invariants.J1-drivable: The journey row produces a wrong and a correct input for every item, and each one performs on screen
invariants.J2-miss-committed: A complete wrong answer is committed as a miss: not credited, no advance, no completion
invariants.J3-miss-reveals-nothing: A miss and its retry do not newly put the answer on screen, in the scene facts or in a host message
invariants.J4-retry-reopens: After a miss the observer can reopen the same item for another try
invariants.J5-credit-moves-on: A credited answer moves to the next item or completes the lesson: no dead end
invariants.J6-completes-once: Answering every item completes the lesson, with at most one submission per evaluated instance
invariants.J7-commit-visible: A committed verdict, retry or advance is confirmed on screen by the real visibility wait: a later render of the same item and phase does not supersede it
invariants.J8-miss-named: On a mode whose catalog entry lists misses, every checked miss names one from that list; a spoken item's known misses are all on the list and a wrong spoken answer records one
invariants.J9-miss-answered: On a mode with levers, every catalog miss is in some lever's answers or in the catalog's unanswered list
invariants.J10-clean-record: A clean program (every item right first time) submits once, and the record says so: passed, score 100, every item first try, no assistance
invariants.J11-recovery-record: The wrong-then-right program submits once, and the record says so: every item solved, each miss in teachingAttempts before its correct try, the score and first-response score set by the first-response gate
